title: Staged Proposed-Knowledge Record (frontmatter)
description: The YAML frontmatter block of a staged record under roster/knowledge-store/proposed-knowledge/. A staged record is the durable, auditable destination for one item an agent listed under `knowledge_steward_handoffs`, and the place knowledge-store-steward records the disposition of that item. This document constrains the frontmatter mapping only. It cannot express the cross-field and cross-file rules that make a record trustworthy -- those are implemented in roster/knowledge-store/src/staged_records.py and are enforced in addition to, never instead of, this schema. This schema also cannot verify that an agent emitted a handoff at all: a handoff is free-form agent output with no machine-checkable emission event. What is checkable is that the staged records which exist are well-formed and internally coherent.
$comment: Rules deliberately NOT expressed here, because JSON Schema cannot express them over a frontmatter-only instance: (1) content_digest must equal sha256(normalised body) -- the body is not part of this instance; (2) status/disposition coherence (status 'proposed' forbids disposition; any other status requires disposition.action == status); (3) the automatic-defer rule (untrusted_instruction_risk true forbids status 'accepted' and forces disposition.action 'deferred'); (4) the source_uri redaction rule over evidence[] and origin values (no absolute local path); (5) id uniqueness across the directory, which is a directory-level property. See staged_records.py. This mirrors schema_validate.py's precedent of supplementary Python checks alongside a JSON Schema document.

id.description: Stable record identifier, KS-YYYYMMDD-slug. Immutable once assigned: a disposition, an audit trail, and any downstream ingestion reference it. Unique across the directory (enforced by staged_records.validate_directory, not by this schema).

title.description: One-line human-readable summary of the proposed knowledge.

status.description: Lifecycle state. 'proposed' means awaiting steward triage and requires `disposition` to be absent; any other value requires `disposition` to be present with a matching `action`.

evidence.description: Citations or file:line references supporting the claim. Must not contain an absolute local path: the same source_uri redaction rule that applies to knowledge citations applies here (roster/shared/knowledge-use-policy.md).

task.description: The task, issue, or pull request the observation came from.

artifact.description: The artifact the observation is about, as a repository-relative path or equivalent non-local reference.

revision.description: The exact revision observed, so the claim stays point-in-time attributable.

origin.$comment: additionalProperties is deliberately left open here while the top level is closed, matching the canonical spec, which closes the top-level key set only. Tighten in a follow-up if origin extensions prove undesirable.
origin.description: Provenance of the observation. All three values are subject to the same no-absolute-local-path redaction rule as evidence[].

proposed_classification.description: The classification the proposing agent believes applies. A proposal, not an authorization: the steward records the classification actually used in disposition.classification_used.

source_scope.description: The project/tenant scope the knowledge belongs to, so an ingestion carries a project-identifying --source rather than defaulting into the shared global store unscoped.

sensitivity_notes.description: Sensitivity, residency, secret-adjacency, or redaction concerns. May be empty, but the key must be present so 'nobody considered it' is distinguishable from 'considered, nothing found'.

conflicts_or_staleness.description: Known conflicts with current approved policy, or reasons this may already be stale. May be empty, for the same reason as sensitivity_notes.

recommended_action.description: The action the proposing agent recommends. 'delete' is deliberately absent and is rejected with its own dedicated error, The reason is act-vs-capability for staged records, where delete-staged exists: proposing a deletion and being authorized to perform one are different acts. Over ingested content it is capability absence as well -- delete-ingested was removed in b418031e and never rebuilt. A required deletion escalates to knowledge-store-steward and an authorized human rather than being recorded as a staged-record action.

untrusted_instruction_risk.description: Whether the source material contains anything that could act as an instruction if retrieved. Boolean true/false, or the string 'unknown' when it was not assessed. true triggers the automatic-defer rule (enforced in staged_records.py): status must not be 'accepted' and any disposition.action must be 'deferred'.

staged_by.description: The actor that converted the free-form knowledge_steward_handoffs item into this record. Names who did the conversion; it does not and cannot attest that a handoff was emitted.

content_digest.description: Lowercase sha256 hex of the normalised record body. Compute it only with staged_records.compute_digest(body) so the digest can never be computed two ways.

action.description: The steward's decision. Must equal the record's `status`.

reason.description: Why the steward decided this. Non-empty: an unexplained disposition is not an audit trail.

classification_used.description: The classification actually applied, which may differ from proposed_classification.

diverged_from_proposal.description: Whether the disposition departed from what the proposing agent recommended.

decided_by.description: The deciding actor. Authorship/approval separation still applies: the actor in staged_by is not thereby authorized to approve its own record.

disposition.$comment: additionalProperties left open for the same spec-literal reason as origin.
disposition.description: Present only once dispositioned. Absent while status is 'proposed'.
